progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: Particle model, reactants/products and reaction rate. Remind students that dissolved molecules are mixed through liquid; explain rate as movement per time before comparing rates.
progression.startsWith: Recognisable sealed sparkling drink, left at constant temperature long enough to settle.
progression.stopsAfter: Explain continuing balanced exchange, stable but not necessarily equal amounts, a static mechanical contrast and open/closed matter boundaries.
progression.nextLesson: How a reversible chemical reaction approaches equilibrium.

teaching.task: A sealed sparkling drink looks steady. What still moves?
teaching.causalExplanation: CO2 leaves and enters liquid. Matching average gains and losses keep the amount steady. Opening lowers gas available to return, so leaving exceeds returning.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Follow the same sparkling bottle. Explain dissolved and rate plainly. Clear earlier reasoning before the next stage.
teaching.openingDecision: A sealed sparkling drink looks steady. What still moves?
teaching.understandingCheck: Infer the return count from 60 departures and unchanged120 over repeated10-second intervals; explain whether exchange stopped.
teaching.curriculumScope: Candidate contribution to the 2017 Chemistry Stage 6 static/dynamic and open/closed action. Not a complete practical or action approval.
